input.quote: 15.16 Nonsolicitation. During the Term and for a period of [***] thereafter, neither Party shall solicit an employee of the other Party who is or has been involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder to terminate his or her employment and accept employment or work as a consultant with the soliciting Party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein shall restrict or preclude the Parties' right to make generalized searches for employees by way of a general solicitation for employment placed in a trade journal, newspaper or website.
input.rationale: § 15.16 sits at our fallback position: the non-solicit is fully mutual (binding SFJ equally), is limited to employees who are or have been involved in the performance or oversight of the development activities (not all personnel), prohibits only active solicitation to leave (there is no "no-hire" or "employ or engage" restriction), and carries an express general-advertising carve-out for generalized searches via trade journal, newspaper or website. No other non-solicit or no-hire language appears elsewhere in the document. Two minor sub-elements short of preferred, noted but not flagged: the tail duration is redacted ([***] after the Term) so it cannot be confirmed as 12 months, and there is no separate express carve-out for unsolicited approaches — though the solicitation-only formulation largely achieves that effect. If the redacted tail turns out to exceed 24 months, that would move the clause into walk-away territory and should be revisited.
